scenario: A tmpfs mount whose super options carry no quota key at all (no quota, usrquota, grpquota and no *_hardlimit key) is visibly quota-disabled, not unknown and not enabled.

fixture.mountinfo:
1 0 259:3 / / rw,relatime shared:1 - ext4 /dev/nvme0n1p3 rw
2 1 259:3 / /proc rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime shared:5 - proc proc rw
3 1 259:3 / /sys rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime shared:7 - sysfs sysfs rw
30 1 0:24 / /run rw,nosuid,nodev,relatime shared:9 - tmpfs tmpfs rw,size=4029068k,nr_inodes=4029068,mode=755,inode64
31 30 0:52 / /run/user/1000 rw,nosuid,nodev,relatime shared:10 - tmpfs tmpfs rw,size=1622560k,nr_inodes=405640,mode=700,uid=1000,gid=1000,inode64

rationale: Contract section C2 quota-classification table, tmpfs rows: 'tmpfs | any of quota,usrquota,grpquota or a key ending _hardlimit | enabled | enforced | tmpfs_quota_option' and 'tmpfs | none of them | disabled | n/a | tmpfs_quota_options_absent'. The contract defines the option source as the super options, i.e. the last mountinfo field, comma-split with the key being the text before '='. The covering tmpfs mount here (/run/user/1000) has super options 'rw,size=1622560k,nr_inodes=405640,mode=700,uid=1000,gid=1000,inode64', whose keys are rw, size, nr_inodes, mode, uid, gid and inode64. None of them is quota, usrquota or grpquota, and none ends with _hardlimit, so the second tmpfs row applies: quota_state disabled, enforcement n/a, basis tmpfs_quota_options_absent. The size and nr_inodes keys are capacity limits, not quota mechanisms, and must not be read as quota evidence; the contract's tmpfs rule names no other key. Source anchors: S084 (Documentation/filesystems/tmpfs.rst at v7.2, lines 129-143) is the complete list of tmpfs quota mount options - quota, usrquota, grpquota, usrquota_block_hardlimit, usrquota_inode_hardlimit, grpquota_block_hardlimit, grpquota_inode_hardlimit - so no other key could have carried quota state; the same file's size and nr_inodes documentation places them outside the quota option table. S082 (Documentation/filesystems/proc.rst at v7.2, section 3.5, lines 1965-1990) fixes the mountinfo field layout used here: fields 1-6 are mount ID, parent ID, major:minor, root, mount point and mount options, then zero or more optional 'tag[:value]' fields, then the '-' separator, then filesystem type, mount source and super options, which is why fstype is read from field m+2 and the option list from field m+4; the optional shared:N fields in the fixture are the documented optional fields and are skipped. Supplementary kernel anchor outside the S077-S084 registry rows: mm/shmem.c at v7.2 (sha256 eb5d1e9107b287c8d9d2c1dda83aa0e573917d5b0f88dc17b55162f22718cefb) - shmem_show_options at 4877-4894 prints exactly the quota keys ,usrquota, ,grpquota and the four ,*_hardlimit= keys, so a tmpfs without quota options emits none of them, and shmem_parse_one at 4620-4672 is the only place quota_types and the quota limits are set. Mount resolution follows the contract's rule that a candidate mount is one whose mount point equals the realpath, is '/', or is a prefix of the realpath followed by '/', and that the longest mount point wins: for /run/user/1000 the candidates are '/', '/run' and '/run/user/1000' and for /run/user/1000/mori they are '/', '/run' and '/run/user/1000', so both paths resolve to the /run/user/1000 tmpfs mount and the ext4 root, the /run tmpfs and the /proc and /sys mounts are never chosen. The device check compares the chosen mount's major:minor with the path's st_dev, and a tmpfs superblock takes an anonymous block device, major 0 with a per-instance minor (mm/shmem.c shmem_get_tree uses get_tree_nodev, and fs/super.c vfs_get_super uses set_anon_super_fc, which allocates MKDEV(0, dev)), so the fixture gives the mount major:minor 0:52 and both paths st_dev 0:52 and the check is a match rather than a device_mismatch. Verdict precedence (contract C2): no path is enabled and no path is unknown, so the run is exit 0 with finding_id QUOTA_DISABLED. The empty device_links and btrfs_sysfs objects are deliberate: this fixture contains no btrfs mount and no device-mapper link, and neither field is consulted for a tmpfs path. Both path entries give path equal to realpath, so the expectation does not depend on whether the probe echoes the requested path or the resolved realpath.
